articles.title: Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping of the Centromedian Nucleus and Indirect Comparison with Alternate Sequences.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulation of the thalamic centromedian nucleus (CM) is an established therapy for epilepsy and been applied for pain, Tourette syndrome, and disorders of consciousness. Accurate targeting remains challenging because CM is poorly visualized on conventional MRI sequences, necessitating reliance on indirect targeting approaches. Although advanced MRI sequences, such as magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition of two gradient echoes (MP2RAGE) and white matter null (WMn), have been explored, they fail to reliably delineate the boundary between CM and lateral thalamus, a region associated with optimal stimulation outcomes, particularly in epilepsy. Quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) has emerged as a promising technique for differentiating thalamic nuclei based on tissue magnetic susceptibility.
OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate visualization of CM using QSM, assess contrast between CM and adjacent nuclei, and indirectly compare across WMn and MP2RAGE.
METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with solitary cerebral cavernous malformations, not involving the thalamus, who underwent surveillance MRI including QSM (n=24). WMn sequences were obtained from a separate cohort of patients with epilepsy (n=16). MP2RAGE sequences were acquired from healthy individuals (n=24). All sequences were registered to the MNI152 template space and compared with the Morel histological atlas. Normalized intensity differences, contrast-to-noise ratios (CNR), and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) were calculated for CM and neighboring nuclei.
RESULTS: On QSM, CM was hypointense to medial and posterior thalamus and hyperintense relative to motor thalamus. Median CNR on QSM (P<0.05) relative to CM was highest for medial pulvinar (median 2.9, interquartile range 1.6-4.7) and ventral lateral thalamus (1.6, 0.6-2.3). Highest overall CNR was seen on WMn for PuM (3.4, 3.0-4.0). SNR on QSM was highest for anterior pulvinar (2.4, 1.1-3.6) and highest overall SNR was on on MP2RAGE for PuA (20.8, 17.3-24.3). In an indirect comparison across independent cohorts, QSM showed greater lateral thalamic contrast than WMn and MP2RAGE, but lower overall SNR.
CONCLUSION: QSM allows visualization of CM including the lateral border poorly seen on other sequences, and may be useful as a complementary sequence for direct targeting of CM.

articles.title: Sclerotherapy for slow-flow vascular malformations: An international survey of practice patterns and periprocedural management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Slow-flow vascular malformations (SFVMs) are rare congenital anomalies that cause significant morbidity. Currently, no evidence-based therapy exists to improve SFVM symptoms and reduce its relapse in the long-term. Sclerotherapy is central to management and widely practiced, yet comprehensive international data are limited and no standardized guidelines exist. We aimed to evaluate current practice patterns, focusing on sclerotherapy and multidisciplinary care.
METHODS: An international cross-sectional survey was distributed to experts in the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies (ISSVA) network. The questionnaire addressed treatment indications, sclerosant use and availability, anesthesia, coagulation management, risk communication, and case-based decision-making. Responses were analyzed descriptively.
RESULTS: Fifty-two physicians from 16 countries completed the survey. Respondents included interventional radiologists (69%), vascular medicine specialists (15%), and pediatric surgeons (8%) in academic centers (90%). Multidisciplinary consultation was reported by 92% of participants. Ethanol (67%), bleomycin (58%), and polidocanol (52%) were the most accessible, although ethanol was consistently rated as the most dangerous. Sclerosant choice varied by lesion type and scenario. The risks most frequently communicated were skin necrosis (92% for lymphatic malformations and 94% for venous malformations, respectively), pigmentary changes (70% and 75%), and nerve injury (68% and 75%), whereas systemic complications such as cardiovascular collapse (16% and 22%) or death (14% and 22%) were less often discussed. In children, general anesthesia was preferred (90% and 86%), whereas adults received local (49% and 41%) or general anesthesia (47% and 43%). Preprocedural coagulation testing and anticoagulation strategies showed marked heterogeneity, especially for venous malformations.
CONCLUSIONS: This survey demonstrates substantial variability in SFVM management, particularly regarding sclerosant selection, anesthesia, coagulation, periprocedural care, and risk communication, and identifies areas where future prospective and collaborative research will be needed before evidence-based recommendations can be developed.

articles.title: Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging in children: state of the art.
articles.abstract: Whole-body imaging in children was classically performed with radiography, positron-emission tomography, either combined or not with computed tomography, the latter with the disadvantage of exposure to ionizing radiation. Whole-body magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), in association with the recently developed metabolic and functional techniques such as diffusion-weighted imaging, has brought the advantage of a comprehensive evaluation of pediatric patients without the risks inherent to ionizing radiation usually present in other conventional imaging methods. It is a rapid and sensitive method, particularly in pediatrics, for detecting and monitoring multifocal lesions in the body as a whole. In pediatrics, it is utilized for both oncologic and non-oncologic indications such as screening and diagnosis of tumors in patients with genetic syndromes, evaluation of disease extent and staging, evaluation of therapeutic response and post-therapy follow-up, evaluation of non neoplastic diseases such as multifocal osteomyelitis, vascular malformations and syndromes affecting multiple regions of the body. The present review was aimed at describing the major indications of whole-body MRI in pediatrics added of technical considerations.

articles.title: Peripheral limb vascular malformations: an update of appropriate imaging and treatment options of a challenging condition.
articles.abstract: Peripheral vascular malformations encompass a wide spectrum of lesions that can present as an incidental finding or produce potentially life- or limb-threatening complications. They can have intra-articular and intraosseous extensions that will result in more diverse symptomology and present greater therapeutic challenges. Developments in classification, imaging and interventional techniques have helped to improve outcome. The onus is now placed on appropriate detailed preliminary imaging, diagnosis and classification to direct management and exclude other more common mimics. Radiologists are thus playing an increasingly important role in the multidisciplinary teams charged with the care of these patients. By fully understanding the imaging characteristics and image-guided procedures available, radiologists will be armed with the tools to meet these responsibilities. This review highlights the recent advances made in imaging and the options available in interventional therapy.

articles.title: Pericytes as targets in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
articles.abstract: Defective paracrine Transforming Growth Factor-β (TGF-β) signaling between endothelial cells and the neighboring mural cells have been thought to lead to the development of vascular lesions that are characteristic of Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (HHT). This review highlights recent progress in our understanding of TGF-β signaling in mural cell recruitment and vessel stabilization and how perturbed TGF-β signaling might contribute to defective endothelial-mural cell interaction affecting vessel functionalities. Our recent findings have provided exciting insights into the role of thalidomide, a drug that reduces both the frequency and the duration of epistaxis in individuals with HHT by targeting mural cells. These advances provide opportunities for the development of new therapies for vascular malformations.

articles.title: Droplet digital PCR as a first-line detection tool in the genetic diagnosis of vascular anomalies.
articles.abstract: Targeted precision therapies are increasingly used in the treatment of individuals with vascular anomalies (VAs). This increases the need for rapid, accurate and inexpensive genetic diagnosis. Droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) is an alternative to next-generation sequencing (NGS), permitting rapid, highly sensitive interrogation of recurrent pathogenic mosaic variants. We examined the feasibility of ddPCR as a primary diagnostic tool in a large cohort of individuals with VAs. Lesional tissue was collected for ddPCR of up to 46 recurrent pathogenic variants across 16 genes associated with VAs. Specimens were assessed on a subset of assays for each individual based on clinical phenotype. Most individuals who had negative ddPCR results went on to high-depth gene panel or deep exome NGS, or Sanger sequencing. Here we report the phenotypic and molecular findings for 78 newly recruited and tested individuals in addition to the 60 individuals already reported from our cohort. The overall diagnostic yield for our cohort when combined with individuals previously reported was 104/138 (75%). Of 138 individuals tested, recurrent pathogenic variants were detected in 71 (51%) on ddPCR. Variants were most frequently identified in PIK3CA (n = 28), TEK (n = 18), GNAQ (n = 12), or MAP2K1 (n = 7). In a further 33 individuals, pathogenic variants were identified on NGS or Sanger sequencing. Our findings indicate that ddPCR is an efficient method achieving a high diagnostic yield in our cohort when used prior to sequencing.

articles.title: Vascular anomalies in pediatrics.
articles.abstract: Vascular tumors consist of lesions secondary to endothelial hyperplasia, incorporating both hemangiomas and less common pediatric vascular tumors. Vascular malformations arise by dysmorphogenesis and exhibit normal endothelial cell turnover. Some anomalies may incorporate multiple areas of the vascular tree. Use of this division has provided a clinically useful method of diagnosis and prognosis, as well as a guide to therapy. It is hoped that with continued investigation into the biology and pathogenesis of these lesions, a more comprehensive molecular classification will soon be developed.

articles.title: Mechanisms of injury and emergency care of acute spinal cord injury in dogs and cats.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To review the literature in regards to the pathophysiology of acute spinal cord injury, and to describe current concepts in regards to patient assessment, diagnostic, and therapeutic measures with a special emphasis on emergency and critical care considerations.
ETIOLOGY: Acute spinal cord injury occurs in 2 phases. The primary injury occurs at the time of initial injury and may include intervertebral disk herniation, vertebral fracture or luxation, penetrating injury, and vascular anomalies such as fibrocartilaginous embolic myelopathy. Secondary injury occurs following primary injury and is multifactorial encompassing numerous biochemical and vascular events that result in progression of injury.
DIAGNOSIS: The diagnosis is based on history and physical examination findings. A neurologic examination should be performed following initial patient assessment and stabilization. Further diagnostics to characterize acute spinal injury include radiographs and advanced imaging modalities such as myelography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging.
THERAPY: Initial treatment should focus on addressing the patient's cardiovascular and respiratory system. Supportive measures to support systemic perfusion are vital to minimizing secondary injury. Specific therapy toward minimizing secondary injury in veterinary medicine remains controversial, especially in regards to the utilization of methylprednisolone. Other therapies are either in need of additional research or have failed to document clinical difference.
PROGNOSIS: The prognosis for acute spinal injury is varied and is dependent upon the presence of concurrent trauma, location, and type of primary injury sustained, and extent of neurologic impairment at the time of initial presentation. The etiology of the underlying trauma is of great importance in determining prognosis and outcome. Loss of deep pain is generally accepted as a poor prognostic indicator; however, even these patients can recover depending on their response to treatment.

articles.title: Current practices in elective embolisation: insights from a UK national cross-sectional survey.
articles.abstract:
AIM: The aim of this study was to evaluate the national landscape of elective embolisation services in the UK and identify factors affecting service delivery and expansion.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey comprising 19 structured questions exploring the current provision of arterial and venous elective embolisation procedures, service capacity, resource availability, and training was distributed to approximately 1,000 members of a national society in March 2025. Quantitative and qualitative analyses were performed.
RESULTS: Eighty-five responses from 54 UK National Health Service (NHS) Trusts were analysed, predominantly from consultant interventional radiologists (85%), working in tertiary centres (62%), district general hospitals (24%), or both (14%). Elective arterial and venous embolisation procedures were widely performed, most commonly uterine artery (94%), renal angiomyolipoma (92%), visceral aneurysm (89%), and varicocele (98%) embolisation. Tumour, type II endoleak, prostate artery, and arteriovenous malformation embolisation were performed significantly more frequently in tertiary centres (P < .05). Most reported access to day-case beds (87%) and clinic time (84%), although provision was frequently perceived as insufficient. While 63% expressed a desire to expand services, key barriers included funding (55%), inadequate referral pathways (45%), bed capacity (39% day-case; 37% inpatient), emergency workload (36%), and workforce shortages (36% radiologists; 36% nurses/radiographers). Qualitative feedback highlighted resource limitations, regional disparities, and the need for more flexible training pathways.
CONCLUSION: Sustainable expansion of elective embolisation across the UK requires clinically integrated interventional radiology (IR) services, protected capacity, infrastructure and workforce investment, regional networks, standardisation, flexible training, and systematic evaluation.

articles.title: Effective combined immunotherapy for severe hemolytic disease of the fetus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Maternal anti-Kell and anti-Rhesus D-alloimmunization cause severe hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDF) by crossing the placenta, leading to anemia and hydrops fetalis. Early-onset HDF from anti-K and anti-RhD alloimmunization often requires multiple, early intrauterine transfusions (IUTs), with higher complication rates and decreased sensitivity after the first intervention. Mortality remains high.
CASE REPORT: We report the successful treatment of three pregnant women with high-titer red cell alloantibodies-two with anti-K and one with anti-RhD-during the first trimester, a period with otherwise limited therapeutic options. We applied a novel triple therapy consisting of immunoadsorption (IA), high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), and rituximab (Rtx) (IIR). This approach resulted in a marked reduction of antibody titers: anti-D decreased from 1:1024 to 1:16, and anti-K from 1:8192 and 1:2048 to 1:32, respectively. One patient presented at 19 weeks of gestation with fetal hydrops, severe anemia, and thrombocytopenia. IIR reduced the need for invasive procedures (intrauterine transfusions) and led to resolution of fetal thrombocytopenia. In the remaining two high-risk cases, IIR prevented the onset of fetal anemia. All neonates were delivered healthy and without anemia.
CONCLUSION: This case series presents a novel, safe personalized prophylactic and therapeutic approach that may delay anemia onset and reduce invasive procedures in high-risk patients with limited options and resulted in healthy neonates without apparent comorbidities.

articles.title: [Neonatal Hyperbilirubinemia - Bridging the Care Gap in the Early Neonatal Period].
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kernicterus resulting from excessive bilirubin concentrations can be effectively prevented by early diagnosis and therapy. The postnatal rise of bilirubin peaks at a time of life most newborn infants have been discharged home while the next scheduled well baby visit is several weeks ahead.
AIM: Evaluating a post-discharge bilirubin follow-up program established in 2010.
METHODS: Retrospective analysis of newborns seen 2010-2024 at the Berlin University Medical Center bilirubin outpatient clinic, exchange transfusions performed in the same time period, and infants admitted for phototherapy in 2022.
RESULTS: The median annual number of infants consulting the outpatient clinic was 616 in 2010-2016, as compared to 1858 in 2017-2024. In 2022, 6% of newborns seen at the outpatient clinic were admitted for treatment of hyperbilirubinemia at a median age of 6 [5-7] days, with a total serum bilirubin concentration of 20.5 [19.3-21.4] mg/dl). The 2 top indications for the 81 exchange transfusions performed in 78 patients were rhesus incompatibility (n=44; 56%) and gestational alloimmune liver disease (n=24; 31%). The bilirubin level immediately prior to exchange transfusion was 15.5 [12.5-20.0] mg/dl (highest measured value 38.1 mg/dl).
CONCLUSION: A post-discharge program attached to a neonatal unit can effectively bridge the gap in care between discharge and scheduled well-baby visits several weeks ahead. A mandatory U2a could standardize follow-up care for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia in the future.

articles.title: Refractory Anti-HMGCR Necrotizing Myopathy With Progressive Hypercapnic Respiratory Failure Responsive to a JAK Inhibitor.
articles.abstract: Immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) associated with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (HMGCR) antibodies is a rare condition often associated with statin use. It typically presents with proximal weakness and markedly elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels and is often refractory, requiring long-term immunotherapy. Respiratory involvement is uncommon but can be life-threatening. Herein, we report the case of a 73-year-old woman with long-standing anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM, refractory to glucocorticoids, methotrexate, azathioprine, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg), rituximab, and plasma exchange (PLEX), who presented with progressive hypercapnic respiratory failure. Despite ongoing treatment with IVIg, PLEX, and high-dose glucocorticoids, the patient's respiratory function worsened, and she required mechanical ventilation (MV). The addition of tofacitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, coincided with marked clinical improvement, discontinuation of MV, and successful transition to room air. The patient continued to do well on this therapy, with improvement in muscle strength until outpatient discharge. The clinical benefit of JAK inhibition has been reported in dermatomyositis, overlap myositis, and anti-MDA5-positive disease, particularly in refractory cases with pulmonary or systemic involvement-but has not been described in the setting of refractory IMNM. In our patient, who had exhausted multiple conventional therapies and PLEX, the rapid clinical improvement after JAK inhibition strongly suggests a therapeutic effect and highlights the need for future studies of JAK inhibitors in IMNM.

articles.title: Sevoflurane-associated diffuse alveolar hemorrhage: A rare cause of postoperative dyspnea. Case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) is a rare, life threatening, early post-operative pulmonary complication of inhaled anesthetics, which are used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia. It refers to hemorrhage originating from pulmonary microcirculation. It presents with hemoptysis, anemia, diffuse lung infiltration, and acute respiratory failure. Common causes are systemic vasculitis, Collagen vascular disease, Bone marrow transplantation, Drugs, and idiopathic conditions. Treatment ranges from supportive care and withdrawal of offending drugs to high-dose steroids, immunosuppressants, and plasmapheresis. Sevoflurane induced diffuse alveolar hemorrhage is a rarely reported entity in the literature that clinicians should be aware of and consider among the post-operative causes of dyspnea while ruling out other etiologies. We present a literature review over sevoflurane induced diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and a case involving a young otherwise healthy patient who underwent surgery for metatarsal fractures under general anesthesia, but diffuse alveolar hemorrhage developed after sevoflurane inhalation in the postoperative period.

articles.title: Therapeutic Plasma Exchange in Pediatric Patients: A Multi-Institutional Landscape Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric evidence for therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) is largely small, single-center cohorts; there is no prior large-scale age-stratified outcomes assessment. Using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, we identified 3744 patients ≤ 17 years old undergoing an index TPE procedure, stratified into four age groups (≤ 1, 2-5, 6-12, and 13-17 years). ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes recorded 30 days prior to the index procedure were mapped to American Society for Apheresis Categories I-III indications; three high-prevalence nonspecific codes were tracked separately. All-cause mortality at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year was assessed. All-cause mortality decreased with increasing age at every time window: 30-day mortality ranged from 16.8% (≤ 1 year) to 4.3% (13-17 years, p < 0.0001). Infant mortality risk was concentrated disproportionately in the first 90 days postprocedure. Sex distribution shifted from a slight male predominance in infancy and early childhood (55%-56% male) to a female predominance in adolescence (55% female, p < 0.0001). Leading specific indications were autoimmune encephalitis (10%), sepsis with multiorgan failure (9%), renal transplant rejection (6%), acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (5%), Guillain-Barré syndrome (5%), and myasthenia gravis (4%); nonspecific diagnosis codes were each individually more prevalent than any single ASFA-mapped indication. This is the first large-scale, age-stratified, multi-institutional characterization of pediatric TPE. We identified an inverse relationship between age and all-cause mortality, a sex-distribution shift in adolescence, and an indication landscape dominated by nonspecific diagnosis codes. These findings offer age-stratified benchmarks for clinical counseling and hypothesis generation.

articles.title: Localized hydrogel depots for CAR-T cell therapy in solid tumors: materials design, cellular fitness and translational deployment.
articles.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy is less effective in solid tumors than in selected hematologic malignancies because vascular, stromal, spatial, and immunosuppressive barriers restrict cell delivery and function. Local hydrogels and related biomaterials can convert a transient administration into a spatially organized depot, but their benefit depends on more than polymer identity. This review therefore combines a scenario-driven framework-depot versus bolus, intratumoral versus peritumoral placement, unresected versus postsurgical disease, and cell-loaded versus cell-free support-with a materials-centered analysis of formation, administration, time-dependent mechanics, architecture, degradation, biochemical presentation, and manufacturing. Direct evidence is distinguished from adjacent mechanistic evidence and design hypotheses. Across the available studies, the best-supported functions are improved delivered-cell recovery, regional persistence, controlled presentation of supportive cues, and enhanced antitumor activity in selected preclinical models. By contrast, universal material-property optima, clinically validated hydrogel-CAR-T products, and cryopreservation of a final cell-loaded depot have not been established. We define practical tests for gelation and device compatibility, productive egression, material-to-cell fitness, component attribution, and integrated-product safety. A materials-focused comparative table and a 30-study evidence map separate measured values from inferred mechanisms and identify where CAR-T cells were directly loaded, administered separately, manufactured in a matrix, or generated in situ. The resulting framework emphasizes that successful platforms must coordinate material behavior, CAR-T quality, anatomical placement, and clinical workflow rather than maximizing retention or chemical complexity alone.

articles.title: Cinchonidine Ameliorates Traumatic Brain Injury-Related Neurobehavioral Deficits via the SRC/RAF1/NF-κB Pathway to Attenuate Mitochondrial Dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Cinchonidine (CD), a metabolite derived from gut microbiota, shows promise in protecting against traumatic brain injury (TBI), where mitochondrial dysfunction is a key driver of secondary damage. Using a mouse model of controlled cortical impact (CCI) and an in vitro primary neuron injury model, CD administration resulted in improved physiological status (weight recovery, stabilized heart rate) and behavioral outcomes (increased travel distance and speed) in TBI mice. Histological analysis showed reduced hippocampal neuronal damage, decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (interleukin‑1β, interleukin‑6, and tumor necrosis factor‑α), and upregulated blood-brain barrier tight-junction proteins (Claudin-5, Occludin, zonula occludens‑1). Mitochondrial function was improved, evidenced by increased mitochondrial DNA copy number, elevated expression of translocase of outer mitochondrial membrane 20 and cytochrome c oxidase subunit IV, and restoration of mitochondrial membrane potential. In addition, CD attenuated TBI-induced changes in mitochondrial dynamics and biogenesis, restoring the phosphorylated dynamin-related protein 1 (p-DRP1)/DRP1 ratio and the expression of mitofusin 1/2 (MFN-1/2) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), while reducing mitochondrial DRP1. Network pharmacology identified proto‑oncogene tyrosine‑protein kinase Src (SRC) as a key target, validated by stable binding in molecular docking and drug affinity responsive target stability assays. Furthermore, cellular thermal shift assays demonstrated a direct interaction between CD and SRC. CD treatment suppressed the activation of the SRC/RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase (RAF1)/nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling axis, as evidenced by reduced phosphorylation of SRC and p65, along with decreased expression of RAF1 and cleaved Caspase-3. Crucially, SRC knockdown mimicked CD's protection, while SRC overexpression abolished its benefits. These findings suggest that CD ameliorates post-TBI mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, and neuronal damage by inhibiting SRC kinase activity and its downstream RAF1/NF-κB signaling pathway. Thus, CD may represent a promising SRC-targeted neuroprotective strategy for TBI.

articles.title: Androgen Receptor (AR) Expression is Associated with an Immune-Cold Phenotype and Reduced Response to Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in ER-Positive/HER2-Negative Breast Cancer.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have limited efficacy in estrogen receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+/HER2-) breast cancer, and the mechanisms underlying immune resistance remain unclear. The androgen receptor gene (AR), expressed in a substantial proportion of ER-positive tumors, has been implicated in tumor biology; however, its role in the tumor immune microenvironment and immunotherapy response is not well understood.
METHODS: We investigated the association between AR expression, transcriptome-derived immune cell-associated signatures, and response to ICIs in 4046 patients with breast cancer across five cohorts with bulk transcriptomic data and two cohorts with single-cell transcriptomic data.
RESULTS: High AR expression was consistently associated with reduced transcriptome-derived tumor-infiltrating leukocyte scores across multiple ER+/HER2- cohorts. Specifically, signatures associated with cluster of differentiation (CD)-8+ T-cell subsets, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages were significantly reduced in AR-high tumors, indicating a transcriptionally immune-suppressed tumor microenvironment. In the I-SPY2 cohort, AR-high tumors demonstrated significantly lower pathological complete response rates after neoadjuvant ICI therapy. Furthermore, AR expression showed a predictive performance for ICI response that was superior to that with programmed cell death protein-1 and programmed cell death ligand-1 (area under the curve 0.82 vs. 0.73 and 0.60, respectively). Interestingly, single-cell analysis revealed that AR expression across multiple cell types, including epithelial, endothelial, and myeloid, was associated with reduced ICI responsiveness. Additionally, AR inhibition using enzalutamide was associated with increased signatures associated with CD8+ T cells, dendritic cells, and M1 macrophages.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that AR expression is associated with an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and reduced response to ICIs in ER+/HER2- breast cancer.

articles.title: Bidirectional Regulatory Mechanisms of T cell-microglia Interactions in Cerebral Ischemic Disease: Molecular Crosstalk, Experimental Techniques and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemic diseases, such as ischemic stroke (IS) and vascular dementia (VaD), are major causes of neurological disability and mortality. Neuroinflammation acts as a pivotal driver of secondary brain injury, mediated by intricate bidirectional interactions between peripheral T cells and central nervous system (CNS)-resident microglia. This review delineates the molecular mechanisms underlying T cell-microglia crosstalk in cerebral ischemia, emphasizing their dual roles in exacerbating neurotoxicity and promoting repair. Direct interactions involve antigen presentation via MHC-TCR engagement and co-stimulatory checkpoints (e.g., CD80/CD86-CD28, PD-L1-PD-1), which regulate T cell activation and microglial polarization. Direct signaling through cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-4, IL-17, IL-10) further modulates microglial phenotypes: Th1/Th17 cells drive pro-inflammatory M1 polarization via STAT1/NF-κB pathways, while Tregs/Th2 cells induce anti-inflammatory M2 states through STAT6/SMAD signaling. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell omics reveal spatiotemporal dynamics of these interactions, identifying STAT1/STAT6 imbalance as a critical determinant of neuroinflammatory outcomes. Advanced methodologies, including two-photon intravital microscopy and microfluidic blood-brain barrier (BBB) models, enable real-time visualization of immune cell trafficking and synaptic communication. Therapeutically, targeting immune checkpoints (CTLA-4, PD-1) or cytokine pathways (e.g., IL-4 mimetics) shows promise in recalibrating neuroimmune responses. However, challenges such as blood-brain barrier impermeability to biologics and interspecies immune heterogeneity necessitate innovative delivery strategies. This review integrates molecular, cellular, and technological insights to propose a framework for precision immunomodulation. By elucidating context-dependent signaling nodes and leveraging emerging tools, the study underscores the potential of harnessing T cell-microglia crosstalk to mitigate neuroinflammation and enhance neural repair, offering transformative avenues for stroke and dementia therapy.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential analysis of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury is a core pathological process underlying further neurological deterioration after reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke. Developing more effective neuroprotective agents is therefore a current priority in neuroscience research. Sertoli cells possess unique immunoprivileged and nutritional support functions within the testes and secrete exosomes that serve as important mediators of intercellular communication, with substantial potential for neuroprotection. This review addresses the protective mechanisms of Sertoli cell-derived exosomes in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. Through a comprehensive literature review, we systematically summarize their neuroprotective effects, including the modulation of immune and inflammatory responses, inhibition of cellular apoptosis, promotion of neurovascular repair, regulation of autophagy, and influence on epigenetic modifications and related signaling pathways. By synthesizing the latest findings in this field, we aim to provide insights into the development and translation of novel neuroprotective strategies based on Sertoli cell-derived exosomes.

articles.title: Activated B cells steer fibroblasts towards a proinflammatory phenotype in giant cell arteritis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is characterized by chronic large-vessel inflammation and remodelling. Within affected arteries, especially in aorta, organized B cell clusters are mainly localized in adventitia, where fibroblasts represent the dominant stromal population. This study aims to investigate fibroblast heterogeneity within these clusters and B cell-fibroblast interactions in vitro as possible contributors to disease chronicity in GCA.
METHODS: Fibroblast phenotypes in CD20+B cell clusters in GCA and atherosclerotic aortic tissues were characterized using immunohistochemistry for fibroblast markers (CD90, PDPN, FAP, CD248, α-SMA) and cytokine expression (IL-6, GM-CSF, BAFF). In vitro, peripheral blood B cells from treatment-naïve GCA patients and healthy donors were stimulated and cocultured with human aortic adventitial fibroblasts (HAoAFs) using either direct cell coculture or transwell systems. To identify relevant molecular pathways for B cell-fibroblast interaction, HAoAFs were pre-treated with infliximab, tocilizumab, baricitinib or upadacitinib, followed by exposure to activated B cell conditioned medium (aBCCM). Protein secretion was assessed by ELISA, Luminex and Olink, mRNA expression was determined by qPCR.
RESULTS: CD90+PDPN+immunofibroblasts mainly localized centrally, whereas CD90+FAP+ and CD90+CD248+fibroblasts mostly located at the border of the clusters. Fibroblasts in/around clusters co-expressed IL-6, GM-CSF, and BAFF. In vitro, HAoAFs cocultured with activated B cells or supernatants thereof upregulated IL-6, GM-CSF, PDPN, and FAP mRNA, and actively secreted IL-6, GM-CSF and BAFF, while type I collagen expression was suppressed. JAK-STAT inhibition abrogated these pro-inflammatory effects, whereas TNF-α and IL-6 receptor blockade did not.
CONCLUSION: Activated B cells drive fibroblasts toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype, potentially sustaining chronic inflammation and disease progression in GCA. JAK-STAT signalling appears central to this effect, highlighting its therapeutic potency at the vascular level in GCA.

articles.title: Spatial polarization of endothelial ICAM-1 governs T-cell exclusion in melanoma.
articles.abstract: An immunosuppressive microenvironment limits therapeutic efficacy in melanoma. Beyond T-cell abundance and function, tumor control depends on T-cell access to malignant cells, yet the vascular mechanisms governing T-cell positioning remain poorly defined. Using RNA sequencing of endothelial cells from tumor cores versus peripheries in a mouse melanoma model, we identified intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) as a candidate regulator of T-cell localization. During tumor growth, T cells shifted from a balanced core-margin distribution to marked exclusion from the core, particularly in T cell-inflamed tumors. This spatial polarization, less evident in other immune subsets, coincided with high expression of lymphocyte function-associated antigen-1 (LFA-1) on T cells. Endothelial ICAM-1 became enriched at the tumor periphery, where vascular integrity was compromised, with increased vascular leakage and reduced pericyte coverage. ICAM-1 blockade restored T-cell infiltration, enhanced effector activity, and delayed growth of immunogenic tumors, and sensitized an immune-refractory tumor to anti-PD-1 blockade. These findings identify endothelial ICAM-1 as a vascular determinant of T-cell positioning and the ICAM-1/LFA-1 axis as a modifiable checkpoint to enhance antitumor immunity and immunotherapy efficacy.

articles.title: Surgical management of Rasmussen's encephalitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis of long-term seizure and functional outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Rasmussen's encephalitis (RE) is a rare, progressive inflammatory brain disease often leading to drug-resistant epilepsy and severe neurological decline. While surgery is the definitive treatment, evidence remains fragmented due to the rarity of the condition. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy of various surgical techniques and identify predictors of long-term seizure freedom.
METHODS: We performed a comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. We included studies reporting surgical outcomes in patients with RE. Pooled proportions were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis, and meta-regression was employed to investigate predictors of seizure freedom, including age at surgery and surgical technique.
RESULTS: Thirty-one studies comprising 460 patients were included. The overall pooled rate of long-term seizure freedom (Engel Class I/ILAE Class 1) was 65.0% (95% CI: 53.0%-76.0%). Subgroup pooling demonstrated high rates of long-term seizure freedom following complete hemispheric disconnection procedures, with hemispherotomy achieving 75.0% (95% CI: 63.0%-85.0%) and functional hemispherectomy achieving 66.0% (95% CI: 50.0%-80.0%). However, meta-regression confirmed no statistically significant difference in efficacy between disconnective techniques (p = 0.2243). In contrast, focal or less-than-hemispheric resections demonstrated significantly inferior efficacy (35.0%, p = 0.0086). Meta-regression analysis indicated that earlier age at surgery was a robust predictor of superior long-term seizure outcomes (beta = -0.0383, p = 0.0165), explaining 27.98% of between-study heterogeneity. Shorter disease duration prior to surgery was likewise significantly associated with higher seizure freedom (beta = -0.0412, p = 0.0210). A modest trend toward improved outcomes was observed in recent publication eras. Baseline clinical severity (preoperative EPC, hemiparesis) and complication rates were not significant predictors. Postoperative gross motor function and language preservation were generally stable, ranging from 67.7% to 94.1% and 84-93.1%, respectively.
CONCLUSION: Complete hemispheric disconnection (whether via hemispherotomy or functional hemispherectomy) is highly effective for controlling seizures in RE, whereas focal resections provide inadequate control. Earlier surgical intervention and shorter disease duration significantly improve long-term seizure freedom. These findings support prompt referral for hemispheric disconnection in patients with medically refractory RE rather than delaying surgery with prolonged immunomodulatory trials.

articles.title: AAV-mediated Siglecf elimination on TAMs reverses TMZ therapy-induced T cell dysfunction in glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary tumor of the brain, characterized by extensive intratumor heterogeneity, and exhibits inevitable recurrence despite conventional therapy. This study investigates the immunosuppressive mechanisms underlying GBM recurrence following temozolomide (TMZ) therapy, with a specific focus on macrophage-associated pathways driving immune evasion. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and mass cytometry time-of-flight analyses in orthotopic mouse GBM models, we revealed extensive transcriptional and phenotypic remodeling of the tumor microenvironment after TMZ treatment, including reduced malignant cell proliferation, activation of cytokine-mediated signaling, pronounced T-cell exhaustion, and a shift of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) toward immunosuppressive sialic acid-binding Ig-like lectin F (Siglec-F, encoded by Siglecf) positive subsets. Functional validation demonstrated that expression of Siglec-F inhibited macrophage phagocytosis and enhanced immunosuppression, whereas Siglecf-targeted intervention using adeno-associated virus (AAV) restored T-cell activation and improved antitumor efficacy. Analyses of human GBM datasets confirmed the enrichment of SIGLEC5+ (human homolog of murine Siglecf) TAMs in recurrent tumors, correlating with adverse prognosis. Collectively, our findings suggest a TMZ-induced immunosuppressive reprogramming of GBM microenvironment and implicate Siglec-F/SIGLEC5+ TAMs as potential mediators of immune escape and promising therapeutic targets to overcome chemoresistance.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Metabolic Reprogramming in Macrophages: A Key Driver of Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent synovitis and progressive cartilage and bone destruction. Synovial macrophages are central coordinators of inflammatory signaling, stromal activation, and osteoclastogenesis, yet their pathogenic functions cannot be explained by extracellular cytokine networks alone. Increasing evidence indicates that macrophage activation is coupled to cell-intrinsic mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming. Within the hypoxic, nutrient-variable, and inflammatory RA synovium, macrophages undergo coordinated changes in glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, tricarboxylic acid cycle flux, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production, fission-fusion dynamics, mitophagy, and mitochondrial DNA homeostasis. These alterations reshape bioenergetics while generating metabolites and organelle-derived danger signals that engage hypoxia-inducible factor 1α, nuclear factor-κB, the NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 inflammasome, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes signaling. The resulting metabolic-inflammatory circuits can stabilize pathogenic macrophage states and propagate inflammation to fibroblast-like synoviocytes, endothelial cells, and osteoclast-lineage cells. This review integrates current evidence on macrophage heterogeneity, mitochondrial remodeling, and intercellular signaling in RA. We further evaluate mitochondria-targeted antioxidants, metabolic modulation, restoration of mitochondrial quality control, inhibition of mitochondrial danger-signal sensing, and multistage nanodelivery. Particular emphasis is placed on evidence strength, macrophage-subset specificity, and the distinction between disease-driving abnormalities and compensatory adaptations. Finally, we outline the biomarkers, human-tissue validation, spatial multi-omics, and delivery strategies required to translate macrophage mitochondrial immunometabolism into precision therapy for RA.

articles.title: Microglia and border-associated macrophages play opposite roles in cerebrovascular and leukocyte responses under systemic inflammation in male mice.
articles.abstract: Microglia closely associate with the vasculature, but their roles in leukocyte trafficking and cerebral blood flow (CBF) during systemic inflammation are unclear. We show that sustained systemic inflammation leads to altered microglia-vascular interactions, leukocyte recruitment to cerebral blood vessels and reduced hypercapnia-induced vasodilation. We find that microglia and border-associated macrophages (BAMs) play distinct roles in these processes: while BAM depletion with clodronate increases leukocyte recruitment, microglia/BAM depletion with PLX5622 and the absence of microglia, but not BAMs in CSF1RΔFIRE/ΔFIRE mice, result in markedly reduced leukocyte recruitment. Supporting this, conditional microglial IL-1 deletion inhibits leukocyte recruitment. Unlike BAM depletion, the absence of microglia impairs hypercapnia-induced vasodilation, while in vivo two-photon imaging reveals microglial IL-1α-dependent interactions between leukocytes and penetrating arteries. Accordingly, reduced hypercapnia-induced vasodilation involves endothelial IL-1R1 and microglial IL-1α. Thus, distinct brain macrophage populations exert opposite effects on leukocyte recruitment and CBF through IL-1 dependent mechanisms in given vascular beds in male mice.
